guide_line: Use the Rydberg equation for a hydrogen line.
steps: A hydrogen electron emits light when it falls to a lower n.
The lower level goes first. A swapped pair gives a negative wavelength.
λ comes out in meters. Multiply by 10⁹ to get nm.
Lines that end on n = 2 are the visible Balmer lines.

problems.q: Wavelength in nm for a hydrogen electron falling from n = 3 to n = 2?
problems.why: 1/λ = R (1/2² − 1/3²), then convert meters to nm.
hints: Put the lower n first so the wavelength is positive.
